title: Reactions rearrange atoms
keyIdea: In a chemical reaction, atoms are rearranged into new substances. No atoms are created or destroyed.

kid: In a chemical reaction, the starting substances are called reactants. The new substances are called products. The atoms swap partners, but they are all still there.
When carbon burns in oxygen, one carbon atom joins two oxygen atoms. Together they make carbon dioxide, CO₂. There is 1 carbon atom before and after, and 2 oxygen atoms before and after.
adult: Because every atom is still there, the total mass of the products equals the total mass of the reactants. This is the particle-level reason for conservation of mass.

Particle diagrams show this well. Draw 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O. On the left there are 4 hydrogen atoms and 2 oxygen atoms. On the right there are 4 hydrogen atoms and 2 oxygen atoms. Only the partners have changed.

familyTip: Use coloured sweets or building bricks as atoms. Build the reactants, then rebuild them into the products without adding or removing any.

practice.prompt: In a chemical reaction, what happens to the atoms?
choices: They are rearranged into new substances
practice.explain: The same atoms join up in new ways.

practice.prompt: {=3*k} g of magnesium reacts completely with {=2*k} g of oxygen to make magnesium oxide. What mass of magnesium oxide forms, in g?
practice.hint: All the atoms end up in the product.

practice.prompt: In C + O₂ → CO₂, how many oxygen atoms are on each side?
choices: 2 on the left and 1 on the right

practice.prompt: A reaction makes {n}H₂O. How many oxygen atoms must the reactants contain?
practice.explain: {n} × 1 = {n} oxygen atoms. Atoms are not created or destroyed.

practice.prompt: What are the starting substances in a reaction called?
practice.explain: Reactants go in; products come out.

pool.prompt: {=4*k} g of hydrogen reacts with {=32*k} g of oxygen to make water. What mass of water forms, in g?
The products of a reaction contain {n} carbon atoms. How many carbon atoms were in the reactants?
pool.hint: Atoms are not created or destroyed.

pool.prompt: Why is mass conserved in a reaction?
choices: The same atoms are there before and after
pool.explain: No atoms are gained or lost, so the mass stays the same.

pool.prompt: In 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O, how many hydrogen atoms are on the right?
Iron and sulfur are heated and make iron sulfide. Which is true?
choices: It is a new substance with different properties
It is a mixture you can separate with a magnet
The iron atoms turn into sulfur atoms
pool.hint: A reaction makes a new substance.
pool.explain: Iron sulfide is a compound. It isn't magnetic like iron, and atoms never change element.

pool.prompt: Which of these is a chemical reaction rather than a change of state?
pool.explain: Burning magnesium makes magnesium oxide, a new substance.
